summary: Two players each command a deck representing their squads, playing cards to move, spot, suppress, or attack across a hex battlefield inspired by real WWII skirmishes in North Africa. As units take casualties their cards leave the deck (or go into a wound pile), so your options visibly degrade over the course of a scenario, mirroring the attrition of the fight.
praised: elegant fusion of deckbuilding with a tactical wargame
quick to teach despite deep tactics
criticised: card draw luck can swing a scenario
later campaign missions can feel unbalanced
deck thinning can snowball for the player already ahead

interaction.kind: direct tactical combat and area denial
interaction.detail: Players act on a single shared hex map, using line of sight, suppression, and initiative order to directly block, ambush, or shoot each other's units. Nearly all meaningful state (the map, unit positions, casualties) is shared and contested rather than sitting on a private tableau.

sources: victory points from controlled objective hexes
scoring.how_you_win: Each scenario prints a small set of objective hexes; holding them at the end of a turn scores VP, and the first side to reach the scenario's printed target (commonly 6-9) wins that mission.
